Definition: from G303 (in the sense of reversal) and G2572; to unveil:--open, (un-)taken away.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says the minds of Israel were blinded, for until this day the same veil remains untaken away in the reading of the old testament, a veil done away in Christ — and then, 'we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord.' The veil is taken away in Christ, and the face is uncovered, and the looking itself changes the looker.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the veil is the heart of the gospel: what Moses covered, Christ uncovers, and I do not read the old Scriptures through a veil anymore. The open face beholds the glory of the Lord, and the beholding changes me into the same image — glory to glory, by the Spirit, not by my effort.
